correspondence.component_scope: Eastern initial feeder and upper river corridor
correspondence.finding: The actual eastern endpoint lies on a small south-side approach to an east–west watercourse. The modeled line goes north to that receiving course, then west and northwest around the broad northern bend and southwest toward the eastern Angijurjuk approach. The eastern federal map shows this full river-and-small-lake corridor and surrounding alternative branches. No separate name is established for the initial feeder, and the longer unselected eastern headwater is not substituted for the model beginning.

The selected long westward middle course enters the mapped Angijurjuk lake from the east, crosses its generalized interior and exits toward the western lake chain. Water Survey station 06SA002 identifies Ravn River at the outlet in this same western setting, using Angajurjualuk Lake in its station name. This supports the Ravn receiving identity; it is not treated as proof of a formal lake-renaming date or a complete alias history. The separately listed Mary River is a northern incoming system rather than the selected eastern beginning.

correspondence.component_scope: Western connected lakes and southward Quartz Lake reach
correspondence.finding: West of Angijurjuk the selection follows the connected small-lake and channel corridor through the Ikiqtuq setting, bends southwest and then south through Quartz Lake. The federal western enlargement shows the full connection and distinguishes the large Nina Bang Lake drainage farther east. Some model segments cut across lake interiors or lie locally beside mapped channels because of generalization; lake labels are not extended into river aliases, and no claim is made about every small connecting waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Erichsen Lake transition and lower receiving river
correspondence.finding: South of Quartz Lake the modeled course winds into the northern Erichsen Lake setting and crosses its northeastern lake-to-outlet corridor before continuing southeast. The two selected model fragments meet in this lake setting; that model split is not a formal river-name boundary. The federal fisheries report independently distinguishes Erichsen Lake from the Ravn River downstream of it. The selected route does not follow the separate southward Neergard Lake corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern lower course and coastal ending
correspondence.finding: The final fragment follows the southeastward lake-and-channel corridor from Erichsen to the northwestern shore of Steensby Inlet. The coastal federal view labels the inlet and distinguishes Tariujaq Arm to the east and Neergard Lake to the south. The historical DFO Ravn entry agrees with this terminal region and separately lists nearby Harder and Neergard rivers. No exact present-day mouth channel, tidal limit, shoreline vertex or river continuation inside the inlet is assigned.

The small eastern beginning follows the directly labeled Highrock Creek approach into Fish Lake. The selected generalized line passes through the Fish Lake and Beaver Swamp setting and leaves west along Fish Lake Creek, which joins South Umpqua downstream of the Black Rock/Castle Rock fork setting. Those northern forks, the southern Buckeye/Cliff lake approaches and Jackson Creek farther south are distinct and are not substituted for the selected beginning.

The receiving South Umpqua continues southwest past the Dumont and Jackson creek junction settings, then west through the Tiller/Days Creek corridor. Near the Cow Creek arrival it turns north through the Myrtle Creek and Winston valley to Roseburg. Repeated South Umpqua labels and the distinctive west-then-north shape establish the selected trunk; incoming Cow, Jackson, Myrtle and Lookingglass creeks are not renamed or added as selected tributary fragments.

The short middle mainstem fragment follows South Umpqua from the Roseburg setting northwest to the North Umpqua junction. The city-side Deer Creek arrival is distinct. The model fragment boundaries are not treated as surveyed name-change points.

The separately selected east-to-west tributary is a bounded middle/lower North Umpqua River reach, following the named canyon/trail corridor and western bends to its South Umpqua junction. Its eastern starting point is already within that river corridor; the model does not include the entire North Umpqua headwater system. Little River enters separately from the south and is not the selected side branch.

The shared receiving trunk is labeled Umpqua River. It follows the large northward inland bends west of Sutherlin, then the looping Coast Range course toward Elkton and the long westbound valley along the Umpqua highway to Reedsport. Calapooya, Elk and Smith river/creek arrivals remain separate contextual waterways.

Below Reedsport the selected line bends north and around the broad Gardiner estuary, then turns south along the Umpqua/River channel west of The Point and the Double Cove setting. Its terminal point is near the Army Hill/North Spit shore setting, still upstream of Winchester Bay and the Pacific entrance. This is a generalized estuary centerline, not proof of an exact current navigable channel, shoreline endpoint or full ocean-mouth coverage.

The downstream selected corridor reaches the Esmeraldas city/Pacific setting. OAS/INERHI defines Esmeraldas proper below the Blanco–Guayllabamba union. This model fragment starts farther upstream, at the Quinindé/Blanco setting, so the fragment boundary is not the hydronym boundary.

The northbound route through the La Concordia–Puerto Quito–Rosa Zárate setting corresponds to the receiving Blanco corridor. A model mainstem designation does not extend Esmeraldas upstream over this separately named river.

The southern modeled mainstem approaches the Blanco corridor through Toachi country. The detailed Sigchos sheet directly labels Río Toachi in the selected valley east of Sigchos and west of Isinliví. Only that bounded middle-upper interval is detailed-map supported; southern headwaters and the onward interval toward Alluriquín are not fully resolved.

This is a separate eastern approach to the Blanco junction, not the southern Toachi continuation. The IGM national map supports the upper Blanco branch arrangement, but does not resolve all its upper component names or the entire selected easternmost approach.

The western branch approaches the Blanco at Rosa Zárate through the Quinindé corridor. The DMA charts show the northbound Quinindé setting. The far-western headwater hook in fragment 11654 is not confidently matched throughout and remains material pending, rather than being named Quinindé solely by downstream continuity.

The long eastern branch occupies the Guayllabamba corridor and meets the receiving route upstream of Esmeraldas proper. This is a separate tributary branch; its detailed upper-channel correspondence and internal name limits are not claimed from the small national map.

The southwestern selected beginning lies in the mesa headwater approach north of El Tigre. The mapped channel runs northeast into the directly labeled Río Guanipa corridor and continues east through the oil-field plain toward Guanipa settlement. Río Mería on the west and Río Pao and Río Tigre to the south are separate mapped waterways. The initial minor approach is not assigned an additional hydronym or declared the official source.

Across the sheet join, the selected northeastward river passes the Guanipa/Los Palos Blancos setting and continues south of Aguasay by El Cedral, where Río Guanipa is directly labeled. The western Caris approach, northern Tonoro corridor and southern Ñato/Tigre drainage are distinguishable. The long middle section and its bends correspond to the receiving Guanipa route rather than to a similarly named settlement or the neighboring Tigre.

The modeled route bends east and then northeast through the Tonoro receiving vicinity and remains south of the separate Amana route and Maturín. The chart depicts branching wetland waters and a marsh fringe farther east. Regional corridor correspondence is retained without claiming that every generalized model vertex follows a specific small wetland channel.

The lower selected course follows the broad channel explicitly labeled Río Guanipa, bends northward and then eastward before its final northward approach to the western side of Boca Bagre. This is the marsh-fringed Guanipa coastal arrival near Isla Venado and west of Pedernales, rather than the separate San Juan mouth or the eastern Mánamo/Pedernales distributary route.

The complete single-fragment selection is covered, with no additional selected tributary fragment. The endpoint is retained as a generalized river-to-coastal-water transition at Boca Bagre in the southern Gulf of Paria setting. The gulf, islands and adjoining marsh/delta channels keep their own feature classes and names; neither present-day flow nor a precise shoreline crossing is inferred from historical cartography.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
